publicReleaseNotes:
Orbit 0.4.4 keeps a truthful record of what each form visitor was shown, gives Reports one list of pages, and carries the changes made since 0.4.3. Orbit now runs on rer 0.2.96.

- **Forms keep a truthful record of what the visitor was shown.** Each submission now keeps the wording, the form's revision and the time. A form with consent wording records that wording and whether the box was ticked. A form without it shows one line saying that sending the enquiry asks for a one-to-one follow-up and does not subscribe the visitor to marketing, and records that line. Settings › Forms shows the record beside the submission. A new contact is marked contactable only when the visitor accepted what the page showed; a contact you had already stopped stays stopped, and sending the same submission again keeps its original record and time. A form published before this update that did not show the follow-up line records no basis, and its new contacts are marked do not contact until you approve and publish the form again. A submission's name, email and company land on the right contact and company, a deal opens in the pipeline and stage you chose, and a deal made by a form names that form.
- **Reports is one list, and each report has its own page.** Reports lists your dashboards first, with your default marked, then your reports: the forecast (in a USD workspace, for a full operator), your saved reports and the built-in reports. New creates a dashboard or a custom report. Each report has its own address, computes when you open it, and recomputes in place when you change the period. The records behind a figure open in the same side panel a dashboard uses, and Report options (saved results, sharing, versions, edit) and the forecast's inputs and history sit there too. You no longer type a report key or a version. A reviewed custom-report preview saves after you change its period, and saving a result keeps Report options open.
- **Closed deals read as closed.** A won or lost deal's header shows its outcome with the date, such as "Won 4 Nov 2026", then the reason, with no Why NOW badge or next action. Records marks won and lost deals, and the board keeps them in their own Won and Lost columns.
- **Undoing a workflow can archive the deals it created.** When you undo a workflow run or version, a deal that workflow created is closed as lost, with a reason naming the undone version, only if nobody has edited it or added a contact, activity, task, message or signal since. Otherwise it is left as it is and listed with who touched it last and when. Undo sends nothing and cancels no scheduled message. Workflow undo is still partly done: the contract keeps it partial, and choosing which owner rules to undo is not complete.
- **Team access.** The Analyst role reads NOW, Records (list and board), deals, contacts, companies, the Brief and Shared records, with no editing controls and with writes still refused. An invited person's local sign-in link opens a styled "Sign in to Orbit" page that lists them to choose. A collaborator's settings name only the owners of the deals they can read. A shared record someone cannot open shows "Record is unavailable", and the message now stays when the list finishes loading after it. Equal access for every operator across every workspace action is not claimed: the contract keeps Equal operators partial.
- **API credentials and agents.** A new guide, Create and use an API credential, gives copyable browser-console steps, and a refused credential request now names the missing or invalid keys. An API credential, active or revoked, cannot approve an exact saved message: the request is refused and no draft, message or mail submission follows. The agent door's guide lists its current tools and resources. The installation owner's agent can save a draft of an existing workflow without activating it, preview and then delete one saved report (the company's policy decides whether it runs or waits for a named person), and read then rotate the private Capture address. The door can also answer a signed pull from Business with its decisions, carrying no arguments, names or record contents, and ends everything it derived from Business when Business stops. The contract keeps each of these agent-door and API-credential clauses partial.
- **Opt-out after an upgrade.** An installation that already had users keeps one-to-one opt-out on, with the retained basis shown in Settings at desktop and phone widths and after a reload. A message approved before the setting existed keeps its original bytes and unsubscribe group, and nothing is submitted to the provider again. Opt-out choices for connected mailboxes, sequences, batches and workflows are not covered by this and stay partial. A signed unsubscribe refuses a new draft to that contact, and refuses the earlier draft's approval at any hour.
- **A complete archive.** Export and restore carry every current category of Orbit data, including captured evidence and Slack routing, notices and deletion history, without secrets or authority. A Slack deletion still pending when a contact was erased restores as held, and nothing is sent until an administrator reconnects and confirms.
- **Smaller fixes.** A next action proposed beside a booked meeting or reply can be accepted after you accept its link, and a stale review still refuses. Notes brought in by an import show the import as their source. A deal-risk citation of an overdue task opens that task, and a citation of a sent message opens its receipt. A connected provider that answers with a redirect stops intake with a plain message. The Sender setup page shows the right hosted commands: a new sender address needs a full deploy. The website recipe's Node example is prepared from the values you fill into the published form. The homepage leads with Orbit as a product.

It updates 0.4.3 in place and keeps every row. It adds one migration, which adds the agent door's replay and decision-feed records and a retention date on its saved calls; nothing else in your data is changed.

migrations.buyerSteps: Adds the agent door's replay-custody and decision-feed tables and a retention date on its saved calls (calls already completed keep 30 days from their recorded start). No existing table is rewritten. No owner action beyond the backup.

agentUpdateInstructions: Update from 0.4.3 in place; never reset or replace the installation. Before updating, stop rer dev and hosted writes and take a private backup outside the checkout: locally with rer export to a file outside the checkout, hosted through Records → Export archive after signing in (it asks for a fresh emailed confirmation). Check out v0.4.4, then rer install (Node 22.20.0, pnpm 10.12.4, rer 0.2.96 pinned exactly) and rer setup locally, or rer deploy --env-file .dev.vars.deploy for a hosted installation: they apply only the pending migration 0075_agent_door_relay.sql and keep the owner, operators, settings and every row, and every applied migration byte stays as it was. No new setting is required. After the update a published form that did not show the one-to-one follow-up line records no basis for new submissions and marks their new contacts do not contact until you approve and publish that form again; check each published enquiry form in Settings › Forms. Reports opens as one list with a page for each report. Afterwards check records, custom fields, forms, drafts, scheduled messages, dashboards and saved reports before resuming.
